steps.action: Upload an existing recording
steps.result: Processing starts; the same finalization pipeline used after live stop produces the final meeting.
steps.note: M01. Source: data-flow Flow 21 and milestone 01. /audio versus /upload is unresolved; these two contracts describe alternatives.

steps.action: Manage tasks across meeting and task views
steps.result: Create, edit, complete, delete, search and filter consistently; an edit promotes a system task to user ownership.
steps.note: M02. Subtasks are displayed; subtask creation is outside this milestone. Source: milestone 02 and task contract.

steps.action: Write and find context-linked notes
steps.result: The same note components serve /notes, meeting detail and people detail, with search, tags and context linking.
steps.note: M03. Source: milestone 03. Note CRUD contracts are absent from the bet contract pages; no endpoint was invented.

steps.action: Start a live microphone recording
steps.result: Permission granted, no concurrent session, ML pre-warmed: the banner changes from Connecting to Recording.
steps.note: M04, M11. Source: data-flow Flow 1. Permission denial is blocking and creates no session. Browser and Core both guard concurrency. Mic only; desktop scope.

steps.action: Speak and follow the live transcript
steps.result: Interim segments appear and are revised in place; final transcript latency target is within 2 seconds of speech.
steps.note: M04, M05. Source: Flow 2. Stream and asynchronous persistence are separate; ML acknowledgement is not durable GCS acknowledgement.

steps.action: Persist audio and release acknowledged local chunks
steps.result: Core stores contiguous sequence ranges; the browser trims only the audio confirmed durable in GCS.
steps.note: M05. Source: audio contract and Flow 2. Frame size is 100ms; GCS segments default to 2 seconds. Highest received sequence must not be treated as highest contiguous stored sequence.

steps.action: Keep recording through a connection loss
steps.result: A degraded banner identifies the gap. Reconnect reports missing ranges and uploads recoverable OPFS audio; final rebuild includes recovered audio.
steps.note: M05. Source: Flows 16, 19 and recording contract. A connectivity resume is not user pause/resume or recovery after tab close.

steps.action: Continue capture when a provider or local buffer fails
steps.result: Recoverable health warnings distinguish ML, transcription, insights, storage and local-buffer failures. Available capture paths continue.
steps.note: M05, M11. Source: Flow 14 and infrastructure. If local buffering is unavailable, healthy direct transport can continue, but offline losslessness is no longer guaranteed.
steps.branch: ML, provider, storage or OPFS failure

steps.action: Write private notes while recording
steps.result: Debounced saves persist meeting notes; finalization preserves them and notes remain editable afterward.
steps.note: M06. Source: Flow 4 and milestone 06. Milestone 06 excludes rich text although the UI design describes a rich-text scratchpad. This route uses meetings.notes, not the reusable context-linked notes table.

steps.action: Follow draft talking points as the meeting develops
steps.result: Draft talking points arrive without interrupting capture and are replaced by final synthesis after stop.
steps.note: M07. Source: Flow 3a. Insight cadence defaults to 30s or 5 final segments, with an action-item fast path.

steps.action: Capture and edit tasks during the meeting
steps.result: Live tasks appear; user-created tasks and edited system tasks become user-owned and survive final reconciliation.
steps.note: M08. Source: Flow 3a, Flows 5–6, milestone 08. The milestone’s field-level ownership wording differs from the contract’s whole-task source promotion.

steps.action: Match a diarized speaker to an enrolled person
steps.result: Matching locks on when confident; bounded unsuccessful attempts exhaust; manual assignments take precedence.
steps.note: M09. Source: Flow 3b and person contract. Speaker-state table names disagree between flow and schema; voice vectors stay service-internal.

steps.action: Correct a speaker label or add a person
steps.result: All segments for that meeting-scoped speaker reflect the chosen person; ML receives the manual state.
steps.note: M09. Source: Flows 7–8. Person records are user-scoped; matching may not override manual assignments.

steps.action: Stop recording and save the meeting
steps.result: Capture stops, ML drains, gaps are repaired, audio is composed and the shared finalization job is published.
steps.note: M04–05. Source: Flow 9. RecordingStoppedEvent confirms capture stopped, not audio composition or finalization. State/outbox writes precede asynchronous work.

steps.action: Rebuild final artefacts from the durable audio
steps.result: Batch transcription replaces live segments, then synthesis and task reconciliation use the final transcript while preserving user work.
steps.note: M01, M04, M08. Source: Flow 11 and task contract. Reconcile system tasks per M08; UI-design and the sequential-pipeline decision still say to skip them. No runtime completion is claimed.

steps.action: Review the completed meeting
steps.result: Headline, summary, topics, talking points, tasks and notes load from durable records after refresh.
steps.note: M01, M04. Source: UI design, Flow 12 and entity read contracts. Processing/failure remain explicit states.

steps.action: Listen to audio and seek from the transcript
steps.result: Playback streams directly from GCS; the active segment is highlighted and selecting a segment seeks to its start.
steps.note: M10. Source: Flow 13 and UI design. A 404 means unavailable/processing; signed URLs last one hour and are refreshed before expiry. Controls include ±15s and 0.5×/1×/1.5×/2×.

steps.action: Receive duration, silence and browser-limit guidance
steps.result: Warn 10 minutes before the default four-hour stop; show no-audio and background-tab behavior; enforce one active recording.
steps.note: M11. Source: Flows 10, 15, 17–18 and UI edge cases. Inactivity timeout is five minutes. Browser capability support is an open question, not certified by this import.
steps.branch: Duration, silence, concurrency or browser limit

steps.action: Restore event state after reconnect or token rotation
steps.result: Replay uses the event cursor; an expired five-minute replay window triggers a full REST re-fetch.
steps.note: Source: infrastructure connection/reconnection semantics. Sticky Core pod affinity remains a known v1 limitation.

steps.action: Discard final write-backs for a deleted meeting
steps.result: Finalization must not recreate deleted meeting data; documented write-backs acknowledge with no new writes.
steps.note: Source: Flow 20 and write-back contracts. Normal delete is blocked during active recording; this covers later post-processing races.
